title: The crossing-number formula for a complete graph with one edge removed
statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n\ge2$ vertices, and let $e$ be any edge. Write $\operatorname{cr}(G)$ for the ordinary planar crossing number: the minimum number of crossing points over drawings of $G$ by simple arcs, with no restriction that edges be straight or lie in prescribed pages. 
**Zheng–Lin–Yang–Cui conjecture.** Is
$$\operatorname{cr}(K_n-e)=\frac14\left\lfloor\frac{n+2}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-4}{2}\right\rfloor$$
for every $n\ge2$?
The displayed quantity is zero for $2\le n\le5$. This is the missing-edge conjecture recorded by Ouyang–Wang–Huang and by the Clancy–Haythorpe–Newcombe survey, Conjecture 2.20. It is distinct from the Harary–Hill formula for $K_n$ and from the bipartite missing-edge problem.
references:
W. Zheng, X. Lin, Y. Yang and C. Cui, On the crossing number of K_m □ P_n, Graphs Combin. 23 (2007), 327–336. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00373-007-0726-z
Z. Ouyang, J. Wang and Y. Huang, The crossing number of the Cartesian product of paths with complete graphs, Discrete Math. 328 (2014), 71–78, Section 1, displays (1.1)–(1.2). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2014.03.011
K. Clancy, M. Haythorpe and A. Newcombe, A survey of graphs with known or bounded crossing numbers, arXiv:1901.05155v5, Conjecture 2.20. https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.05155v5
Attribution to the 2007 paper follows the latter two sources; the original 2007 text was not directly consulted in preparing this record.
